# FG-GIT-0014

| 項目 | 値 |
|---|---|
| HTTP ステータス | 400 |
| 重大度 | info |
| Runbook | なし |
| 発生させるテスト | `pkt_line_rejects_invalid_lengths` |

## 利用者向けメッセージ

- ja: Git のプロトコルとして正しくない要求です。
- en: The request is not valid for the Git protocol.
- id: Permintaan tidak valid untuk protokol Git.

## 原因 (cause)

A Smart HTTP request broke the Git wire protocol before git was started, or forge refused a protocol feature or an object the request wants (an object no ref reaches: removed by a force push or a deleted branch). git itself never saw the bytes. The want refusals reach the client in-band (HTTP 200 with an `ERR` packet), so git prints `remote error:` with this message and the request id.

## 調べ方 (diagnosis)

The log event carries `reason`: `pkt_line` (with `detail`: `length_reserved` for 0001-0003 where not allowed, `length_too_large` over 65520, `non_hex`, `truncated`, `bad_sideband`), `gzip` (the gzip body is corrupt, truncated, or has data after its end), `content_type` (wrong or missing request Content-Type for the service), `content_encoding` (a request Content-Encoding other than gzip or identity), `want_invalid` (an upload-pack `want` line that is not `want <40 or 64 lower-case hex>`), `command_unsupported` (a protocol v2 command other than `ls-refs` / `fetch`, with `command`), `filter_unsupported` (a `filter` naming `sparse`, e.g. `sparse:oid=<blob>`, which would read a blob by id), `too_many_wants` (more non-commit wants than `git.http.max_object_wants`, with `objects`, `max_object_wants`), `want_unreachable` (an upload-pack request wants an object that no ref reaches — ADR-0007 option (a): forge checks every `want` before upload-pack starts and answers with an in-band `ERR` packet; `wants`, `unreachable`, `commits`, `objects` count them, `first_unreachable` is the first such id, `walked` the objects the walk read, `check_ms` the cost of the check), `too_many_commands` (a push with more ref updates than the limit, 1000; `max_commands`), `report_status_required` (a push client without the report-status capability: forge answers refusals in that report), `push_cert` (signed pushes are refused), and for receive-pack (M1 phase 9 MR4, `service=git-receive-pack`): `command_invalid` (with `detail`: `shape`, `object_id` — not the negotiated object format, `unchanged_ref` — old and new equal or both zero, `ref_bytes` — a ref name with control characters, spaces or invalid UTF-8, `capabilities_bytes`, `capabilities_not_first` — capabilities on a later command, `shallow_id`, `special_packet`, `data_after_empty_section` — bytes after git's empty probe request), `capability_unsupported` (with `capability`: a capability forge's receive-pack does not advertise, e.g. `push-options`, `side-band`, an unknown `object-format`), `duplicate_ref` (the same ref twice in one push), `shallow_misplaced` (a `shallow` line after the first command), `git_refused` (git refused a push and its own words — an `unpack` error, an `ng` reason outside git's short ones, a fatal side-band message — were replaced for the client by this code and the request id; the originals are in `git_messages`, e.g. fsck findings such as `missingEmail`). Clients are normally real git; frequent occurrences from one address point at a scanner or a broken proxy that alters bodies.

## 対処 (fix)

Nothing to fix server-side for a broken or hostile client. A git client that hits `report_status_required` or `push_cert` needs a normal `git push` (no `--signed`). A proxy that rewrites bodies must pass them through unchanged.
